I compared it to the ivory charter school cardigan in the same size (and some other colors), also this years model. The ivory one (MAK  like most of the orig style) has slightly wider shoulder seems, thinner fabric, smaller buttons. This charcoal one (diff designer  fervour same style name), has thick ribbed edging, larger buttons, wider body, longer overall and is made of a softer, maybe slightly thicker fabric. For me, they both work. They do fit a little differently. The charcoal may fit me a little better and is a little comfier.Id be interested in seeing more colors of this charcoal version. The larger buttons and thicker ribbing could be toned down a bit, but I would guess most people may not notice. It does feel a little more substantial, but the difference is minimal.bottom line: You probably want this as you can wear it with everything.If the trim/buttons and sizing diff might matter to you check the designer first. If you just squeezed into the fervour style (this), order a size up in the MAK version (ivory, other colors).

So even though the waist is around 35 too large on my, the zipper still ripped off of its seam at the bottom the first time I wore it, since my bust and hips are 10 larger than my waist. I have to be super careful every time I put the dress on, whether over my head or stepping in to it, to make sure I dont rip even more of the zipper off and open the center back seam even more. Ignore the advice to size down!! Measure your waist and select your size based on the Modcloth size guide for your waist measurement. My waist is 33 inches, which is right in the middle of the XL size range, but my 39 inch hip measurement falls in the L size range. I often struggle to choose between an L or an XL, but quickly went for an L this time, given the number of reviews recommending sizing down. The skirt arrived today and it is too tight! The waist is elasticized, but it still measures at a standard L size of around 31 inches. The elastic is a thin band and not very stretchy, so while it does stretch over to fit my waist. it digs in and is quite uncomfortable. Its true that the rest of the skirt is quite roomy and flares out, so if your hips are on the large size you could probably go a size lower than your usual hip size. But beware that the sizing runs true around the waist. I am exchanging the L today for an XL.

I spoke to one of the online customer service reps, a cool service, except, after figuring out my measurements (according to the guide) and telling the rep, she advised I go with a 1x, This was pretty unexpected, as Im usually a 12, and most of the reviews said these pants were a bit stretchy, but I compromised this advise by going down to a 15. Boy, should I ever have listened to myself! the pants were waaaaay too big! I definitely needed an 11, or at the very largest, a 13.To be honest, Im really upset that modcloth has this service that is supposed to help me find the right sizes and then they advise me to purchase as size that was so far off! To make matters worse, I had to pay 20$ in customs fees to get the pants shipped to Canada, and it would cost just as much to ship and return them back to modcloth, so Im now stuck with them! VERY disappointing. That said, I have to give this item at least three stars, because I can tell theyre great quality, and the length was great for me, as a short girl, the length works perfectly as either cropped or fulllength pants.
